correctness.rationale: For a partial identity with support S, comparison of the domains of the two compositions requires x∈S iff f(x)∈S for every x in the domain of f. This condition is sufficient, so the commuting partial bijections are independent restrictions to S and its complement. Counting rank-j partial bijections gives R_m=m!L_m^(0)(−1); cancellation against the number of choices of S gives the two coefficient factors. Their convolution is L_n^(1)(−2) by squaring the ordinary Laguerre generating function, and the empty-set case is consistent. In the Perron formula the ratio at (α,x)=(1,2) versus (0,1) has prefactor e^(−1/2)2^(−3/4)sqrt(n) and exponential factor exp(2(sqrt(2)−1)sqrt(n)); uniform sampling supplies 2^−n. At k=n/2+s with s=x n^(3/4)+O(1), 2sqrt(k)+2sqrt(n−k)=2sqrt(2n)−sqrt(2)s²/n^(3/2)+O(s⁴/n^(7/2)), and [k(n−k)]^(−1/4)=sqrt(2)n^(−1/2)(1+o(1)). The remainder and coefficient equivalents are uniform for bounded x. This yields the local prefactor 2^(1/4)/sqrt(π) and exponent −sqrt(2)x². Compact Riemann sums and the unit integral of the limiting density give tightness and weak convergence, with variance parameter 1/(2sqrt(2)). This proves the limiting law, not a moment limit inferred from numerics. The recorded exhaustive checks are for n≤4 only; the large-n variance and probability ratios are diagnostics. The script and output were inspected, not run.

originality.rationale: The finite count is a direct consequence of the known centralizer split and the sharp probability equivalent is a direct ratio of two Perron evaluations. The conditional local limit is also a mechanical consequence of an existing stronger local-limit theorem that applies here. Let F(z)=exp(g(z))=(1−z)^−1 exp(z/(1−z)), g_j=1+1/j for j≥1, and a_k=[z^k]F. Cantón–Fernández–Fernández–Maciá, Theorem 5.7, makes both F and F² Hayman-admissible: the coefficients of g and 2g are bounded between positive constants, so choose R=1 and β=λ=0 in (5.14). These are strongly Gaussian and their Theorem C gives uniform local Gaussian probabilities. For independent tilted sizes X_r,Y_r with Pr(X_r=k)=a_k r^k/F(r), the exact conditional law given X_r+Y_r=n is the frozen rank law, by cancellation of the tilt. The sum is the Khinchin family of F². The individual mean m(r)=r g′(r)=(1−r)^−2−1 and variance σ²(r)=r m′(r)=2r(1−r)^−3. Set m(r)=n/2, so the sum's mean is n, with variance 2σ² and σ²∼n^(3/2)/sqrt(2). The two individual local probabilities at k and n−k divided by the sum probability at n therefore give (1/(sqrt(π)σ)) exp(−(k−n/2)²/σ²)(1+o(1)) uniformly on compact scaled windows, exactly the frozen limit. This uses the prior uniform LLT for all three factors without a new asymptotic lemma. No prior word-for-word statement of the semigroup experiment was needed for this implication.
